present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

kin.note: N. MURPHY AND MRS. M. FRAUNER ARE HUSBAND AND WIFE, AND THE REGISTER MARRIED THEM. Entry 1 of Father St Cyr's marriage register, at Chicago, 1834: 'N. Murphy' and 'Mrs. M. Frauner', celebrated by J. M. I. Saint Cyr, filed as st_cyr_marriage_001_1 and st_cyr_marriage_001_2 in data/research/church/records/st_cyr_marriages_1834_1839.json. THE DATE IS AT OR BEFORE THE SCENE: they were married on the day this dataset reconstructs. THE GRADE IS WHAT A PARISH REGISTER IS WORTH FOR THE ACT IT RECORDS. The St Cyr register is the contemporary record OF this marriage — the date, the place, the celebrant and both parties by name, written by the priest who performed it — so the relationship is read off a record rather than reasoned to. The rung these two people carry (G2c, inferred) is a ruling about RESIDENCE: a parish register naming somebody is weak evidence that they LIVED in the town and strong evidence that the act happened, and this row claims only the second. THE LIMIT: the reading is transcription_mediated — the Illinois Catholic Historical Review's printed transcription, not the manuscript — and a transcription can mangle a name. It cannot invent a couple. NO IDENTIFICATION IS BEING MADE HERE. Both cards were minted FROM this entry and carry its record id in church_evidence, so the two people this row links are the two people the entry names; nothing is matched by surname. A KINSHIP IS NOT A PLACEMENT: neither household's position, arrival, trade or membership rests on this row.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'murphy_n:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('murphy_n:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.
